name: Akira (G1024) - Ishrath Jahan
description: Challenge 5 Akira profile: 25 unique techniques across 12 selected tactic phases. Matches the delivered TTP mapping using ATT&CK Enterprise v18. Colours represent qualitative confidence in source support, not severity or frequency. Compiled 2 November 2026. Behaviours span different reports/incidents and do not describe one universal attack chain. This layer was generated as JSON, not exported or visually tested in the Navigator UI.

techniques.comment: Valid Accounts - Uses valid VPN or other account credentials for initial access. Sources: S1: https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1024/; S2: https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/cybersecurity-advisories/aa24-109a; S4: https://www.sophos.com/en-us/blog/akira-again-the-ransomware-that-keeps-on-taking

External Remote Services — Uses compromised VPN accounts and remote access services. Sources: S1: https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1024/; S2: https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/cybersecurity-advisories/aa24-109a

Exploit Public-Facing Application — Reported exploitation of internet-facing services; individual CVE and case attribution remain source-specific. Sources: S2: https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/cybersecurity-advisories/aa24-109a; S3: https://blog.talosintelligence.com/akira-ransomware-continues-to-evolve/; S4: https://www.sophos.com/en-us/blog/akira-again-the-ransomware-that-keeps-on-taking

PowerShell - PowerShell used for credential harvesting, privilege escalation and deleting shadow copies. Sources: S1: https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1024/; S2: https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/cybersecurity-advisories/aa24-109a; S3: https://blog.talosintelligence.com/akira-ransomware-continues-to-evolve/

Windows Command Shell - Uses cmd.exe, batch scripts and net commands. Sources: S2: https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/cybersecurity-advisories/aa24-109a; S4: https://www.sophos.com/en-us/blog/akira-again-the-ransomware-that-keeps-on-taking

Domain Account - Creates domain accounts for persistence; administrative username itadm reported in some incidents. Sources: S2: https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/cybersecurity-advisories/aa24-109a; S4: https://www.sophos.com/en-us/blog/akira-again-the-ransomware-that-keeps-on-taking

LSASS Memory - Credential extraction from LSASS, including comsvcs.dll MiniDump activity in Sophos reporting. Sources: S2: https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/cybersecurity-advisories/aa24-109a; S4: https://www.sophos.com/en-us/blog/akira-again-the-ransomware-that-keeps-on-taking

NTDS - Copies NTDS.dit and SYSTEM hive from domain controllers. Sources: S2: https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/cybersecurity-advisories/aa24-109a; S4: https://www.sophos.com/en-us/blog/akira-again-the-ransomware-that-keeps-on-taking

Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets — Scripts used to obtain Kerberos authentication material; do not infer every ticket-forging method. Sources: S1: https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1024/; S3: https://blog.talosintelligence.com/akira-ransomware-continues-to-evolve/

Exploitation for Privilege Escalation - Reported Veeam exploitation and vulnerable-driver activity; paths vary by incident. Sources: S2: https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/cybersecurity-advisories/aa24-109a; S3: https://blog.talosintelligence.com/akira-ransomware-continues-to-evolve/

Disable or Modify Tools - Disables or uninstalls security tools. ATT&CK v18 identifier retained to match the workbook; v20 cross-reference T1685. Sources: S1: https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1024/; S2: https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/cybersecurity-advisories/aa24-109a; S4: https://www.sophos.com/en-us/blog/akira-again-the-ransomware-that-keeps-on-taking

Match Legitimate Resource Name or Location - Uses legitimate-looking file names and locations. Sources: S1: https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1024/; S3: https://blog.talosintelligence.com/akira-ransomware-continues-to-evolve/

Remote Desktop Protocol - RDP used for movement between victim systems. Sources: S1: https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1024/; S2: https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/cybersecurity-advisories/aa24-109a; S4: https://www.sophos.com/en-us/blog/akira-again-the-ransomware-that-keeps-on-taking

Domain Trust Discovery - Enumerates trust relationships using nltest or AdFind. Sources: S1: https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1024/; S2: https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/cybersecurity-advisories/aa24-109a

Remote System Discovery - Finds domain controllers and hosts using network discovery tools. Sources: S1: https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1024/; S2: https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/cybersecurity-advisories/aa24-109a

Archive via Utility - Uses WinRAR to archive data before exfiltration. Sources: S1: https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1024/; S2: https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/cybersecurity-advisories/aa24-109a; S4: https://www.sophos.com/en-us/blog/akira-again-the-ransomware-that-keeps-on-taking
SharePoint - MITRE records access to and download of SharePoint data. Sources: S1: https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1024/

Remote Access Tools - Uses legitimate remote access tools including AnyDesk and LogMeIn. Sources: S1: https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1024/; S2: https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/cybersecurity-advisories/aa24-109a; S4: https://www.sophos.com/en-us/blog/akira-again-the-ransomware-that-keeps-on-taking; S6: https://www.s-rminform.com/latest-thinking/camera-off-akira-deploys-ransomware-via-webcam
Protocol Tunneling - CISA reports tunnelling tools including Ngrok. Sources: S2: https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/cybersecurity-advisories/aa24-109a

Exfiltration to Cloud Storage - Rclone and cloud destinations including Mega are reported. Sources: S1: https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1024/; S2: https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/cybersecurity-advisories/aa24-109a; S4: https://www.sophos.com/en-us/blog/akira-again-the-ransomware-that-keeps-on-taking

Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol - Reported transfers through WinSCP, FileZilla and PuTTY/PSCP; protocols vary. Sources: S2: https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/cybersecurity-advisories/aa24-109a; S4: https://www.sophos.com/en-us/blog/akira-again-the-ransomware-that-keeps-on-taking

Data Encrypted for Impact - Encrypts victim data across Windows and virtualisation platforms. Sources: S1: https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1024/; S2: https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/cybersecurity-advisories/aa24-109a; S3: https://blog.talosintelligence.com/akira-ransomware-continues-to-evolve/

Inhibit System Recovery - Deletes Volume Shadow Copies using PowerShell/WMI commands. Sources: S2: https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/cybersecurity-advisories/aa24-109a; S3: https://blog.talosintelligence.com/akira-ransomware-continues-to-evolve/; S4: https://www.sophos.com/en-us/blog/akira-again-the-ransomware-that-keeps-on-taking
Account Access Removal - MITRE records deletion of administrator accounts before encryption. Sources: S1: https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1024/

Financial Theft - Ransom and extortion activity, retained from the submitted TTP mapping. Sources: S1: https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1024/; S2: https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/cybersecurity-advisories/aa24-109a
